title: MASTARS: Multi-Agent Sequential Trajectory Augmentation with Return-Conditioned Subgoals
claim: Independent, joint, and naive sequential generation each fail on coordination, diversity or coherence; our method achieves all three together.
layout: 5 panels in a row, left-to-right, final panel highlighted with red border
description: A single row of five square 2-D panels labeled (a) Raw trajectory, (b) Independent, (c) Joint, (d) Simple sequential and (e) Ours. Each panel shows three agents' trajectories as dotted paths in red, blue and green, each fading from light to dark along time. Black X marks show landmark positions reconstructed from each agent's observation. In (a) the X marks are spread out. In (b) and (c) they cluster or overlap, and the paths look either uncoordinated or too close to the original data. In (d) the X marks are scattered and don't match the paths. The final panel (e) has a thick red border. Its X marks sit on a consistent set of landmarks that the agents head towards. A thin vertical line separates the raw data from the generated variants. The eye goes first to the red-bordered panel.
caption: Comparison of trajectory generation strategies: Existing strategies struggle to jointly achieve coordination, diversity, and global coherence, while MASTARS satisfies all three. X marks are landmark positions reconstructed from each agent's observation.
abstract: The performance of offline Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) is limited by the quality of the fixed offline dataset, motivating trajectory augmentation. However, augmenting multi-agent trajectories presents a fundamental challenge of the diversity-coordination trade-off: independent generation improves diversity but lacks coordination, while joint generation induces coordination but lacks diversity, reproducing the training distribution. To address this challenge in multi-agent data augmentation, we introduce MASTARS, a novel diffusion-based framework that generates multi-agent trajectories sequentially across agents while enforcing cross-agent consistent coordination via the method of inpainting. MASTARS produces trajectories that are diverse, coordinated and globally coherent. Experiments on various benchmarks such as MPE, SMAC, and SMAC-v2 demonstrate significant performance gains across multiple offline MARL methods.
